**Michael Bayer ([@zzzeek](https://github.com/zzzeek)) wrote:**

that's got to be a bug b.c. it is inconsisent vs. collection.   if b is deassociated from a it should also de-associate a.ab.  happens for a collection and not for the scalar case here.  from another pov assignment of a.b creates the ab so removal of it should deassociate the ab.

**Michael Bayer ([@zzzeek](https://github.com/zzzeek)) wrote:**

`del a.b` also fails

**Michael Bayer ([@zzzeek](https://github.com/zzzeek)) wrote:**

Here is a workaround (not for the "del" part, just the set None part), issue will be targeted at 1.3:


```
import operator


def getset_factory(collection_cls, proxy):

    attr = proxy.value_attr
    _getter = operator.attrgetter(attr)

    def getter(target):
        return _getter(target) if target is not None else None

    def setter(target, value):
        setattr(target, attr, value)
        if value is None:
            # hardcode to the backref since the association proxy
            # isn't giving you the "A" here :(
            target.a = None

    return getter, setter


class A(Base):
    __tablename__ = 'test_a'
    id = Column(Integer, primary_key=True)
    ab = relationship(
        'AB', backref='a', cascade='all, delete-orphan', uselist=uselist)
    b = association_proxy(
        'ab', 'b', creator=lambda b: AB(b=b), getset_factory=getset_factory)


class B(Base):
    __tablename__ = 'test_b'
    id = Column(Integer, primary_key=True)
    ab = relationship('AB', backref='b', cascade='all, delete-orphan')


class AB(Base):
    __tablename__ = 'test_ab'
    a_id = Column(Integer, ForeignKey(A.id), primary_key=True)
    b_id = Column(Integer, ForeignKey(B.id), primary_key=True)

```

**Michael Bayer ([@zzzeek](https://github.com/zzzeek)) wrote:**

i don't think this can be automatic.   it's not a given that deleting an attribute from "AB" should de-associate "AB" itself, because there can be lots of other things from A->AB->X that are *not* deleted, and it's not clear that "AB" is really an "orphan" here based on those things.    I'd have to give you a new option to the association proxy.   or a recipe using an event.

**Michael Bayer ([@zzzeek](https://github.com/zzzeek)) wrote:**

Handle association proxy delete and provide for scalar delete cascade

Fixed multiple issues regarding de-association of scalar objects with the
association proxy.  ``del`` now works, and additionally a new flag
:paramref:`.AssociationProxy.cascade_scalar_deletes` is added, which when
set to True indicates that setting a scalar attribute to ``None`` or
deleting via ``del`` will also set the source association to ``None``.

Change-Id: I1580d761571d63eb03a7e8df078cef97d265b85c
Fixes: #4308
